title: Dependencies Installation and Project Structure Initialization
description: Set up the development environment for Tiny-LR Proxy SFT dataset ranking experiments. The project requires PyTorch with CUDA support, the LLaMA-Factory framework (v0.9.2+) for standardized SFT training with LoRA, Hugging Face libraries (transformers, datasets, peft, accelerate), vLLM for fast inference during evaluation, and the lm-eval-harness for automated GSM8K and MATH-500 benchmark evaluation. The codebase will support training Qwen2.5-1.5B (proxy) and Qwen2.5-7B (target) models across 12 math-domain candidate datasets at multiple learning-rate regimes, plus evaluation and ranking comparison scripts.
summary: Environment fully configured. Venv at .venv (Python 3.12, system-site-packages). Installed: torch 2.9.1+cu129, transformers 4.57.6, datasets 4.0.0, accelerate 1.11.0, peft 0.18.1, trl 0.24.0, vllm 0.12.1, flash_attn 2.8.1, deepspeed 0.18.6, bitsandbytes 0.49.2, lm-eval 0.4.11, seaborn 0.13.2, LLaMA-Factory 0.9.5.dev0 (editable at LlamaFactory/). Project structure created at tlr_proxy_sft/. Both Qwen2.5-1.5B and Qwen2.5-7B models verified in HF cache. GPU smoke test passed on A100-SXM4-80GB: model loading, lm-eval gsm8k dry run, and LLaMA-Factory CLI all working.

title: Data Preparation and Target Model (Qwen2.5-7B) Ground-Truth Runs
description:
Download and preprocess the 12 math-domain candidate SFT datasets from OpenDataArena's scored-data collection, then fine-tune the target model Qwen2.5-7B on each dataset to establish ground-truth downstream performance rankings. These target scores define the gold-standard dataset ordering against which all proxy methods are evaluated. Training uses the LLaMA-Factory framework with LoRA, following OpenDataArena's standardized SFT protocol for Qwen2.5 models. Each dataset × seed combination produces a checkpoint that is evaluated on GSM8K and MATH-500 to yield the target score S_t(D_i).

Reference: "OpenDataArena: A Fair and Open Arena for Benchmarking Post-Training Dataset Value" | https://github.com/OpenDataArena/OpenDataArena
summary: Ran all experiments ourselves. Downloaded and preprocessed 12 math-domain datasets (50k samples each) from OpenDataArena scored-data. Fine-tuned Qwen2.5-7B with LoRA (rank=16) for 2000 steps on each dataset x 3 seeds = 36 runs using LLaMA-Factory + DeepSpeed ZeRO-3 on 8x A100 GPUs. Evaluated all 36 checkpoints on GSM8K (exact_match) and MATH-500 (math_verify) using lm-eval + vLLM. Top datasets by composite score: dart-math-hard (0.603), openmathinstruct-2 (0.592), R1-Distill-SFT-math (0.482). Bottom: Maths-College (0.175), AM-Thinking (0.146). Results in EXPERIMENT_RESULTS/target_ground_truth/ and tlr_proxy_sft/results/target_ranking.json.

title: Standard-LR Proxy SFT on Qwen2.5-1.5B (Condition A)
description:
Fine-tune the proxy model Qwen2.5-1.5B on each of the 12 candidate math datasets using a standard SFT learning rate (5e-5), then evaluate on GSM8K and MATH-500 to produce proxy scores S_p(D_i; eta_std). This is the primary baseline condition (Condition A): the conventional proxy-model approach practitioners would typically use. The resulting dataset ranking is compared against the target model's ground-truth ranking to compute PDA and Spearman correlation. Training protocol mirrors the target runs except for model size (1.5B vs 7B) and training budget (500 steps vs 2000 steps), following the proposal's proxy configuration.

Reference: "OpenDataArena: A Fair and Open Arena for Benchmarking Post-Training Dataset Value" | https://github.com/OpenDataArena/OpenDataArena
summary: Ran all experiments ourselves. Fine-tuned Qwen2.5-1.5B with LoRA (rank=16, LR=5e-5) for 500 steps on 12 datasets x 3 seeds = 36 runs using LLaMA-Factory on 8x A100. Merged LoRA adapters and evaluated on GSM8K (exact_match) and MATH-500 (math_verify) using lm-eval + vLLM. Ranking agreement with target (Qwen2.5-7B): PDA=0.7121 (95% CI [0.6061, 0.8182]), Spearman rho=0.5944 (p=0.0415), Top-1 match=True (dart-math-hard). Top proxy datasets: dart-math-hard (0.505), mathplus (0.432), R1-Distill-SFT-math (0.338). Results in EXPERIMENT_RESULTS/proxy_std_baseline/ and tlr_proxy_sft/results/proxy_std_ranking.json.

title: Training-Free Base-Model NLL Baseline on Qwen2.5-1.5B (Condition C)
description:
Compute the base-model negative log-likelihood (NLL) of the proxy model Qwen2.5-1.5B on each of the 12 candidate datasets WITHOUT any fine-tuning. This training-free baseline (Condition C) measures how well each dataset 'fits' the base model's pretrained distribution — datasets with lower NLL are a better distributional match. The NLL ranking is compared against the target model's ground-truth ranking to establish whether a zero-cost signal can predict dataset value. This also serves as a critical control: if the Tiny-LR proxy's ranking is no better than base-model NLL, it suggests the tiny-LR proxy is effectively 'not training' and merely reflecting base-model fit.

Reference: "The Best Instruction-Tuning Data are Those That Fit" | https://github.com/facebookresearch/GRAPE
summary: Ran experiment ourselves. Computed base-model NLL of Qwen2.5-1.5B (bf16, no fine-tuning) on all 12 datasets (50k samples each), scoring assistant response tokens only with cutoff_len=4096. Processed on 4x A100 GPUs in ~3.6 hours. NLL ranking (lower=better fit): mathplus (0.41), openmathinstruct-2 (0.44), numinamath-cot (0.52), R1-Distill-SFT-math (0.57), numinamath1_5 (0.63), QwQ-LongCoT-130K-math (0.64), Magpie-Reasoning-V2-250K-CoT-QwQ-math (0.73), AM-Thinking (0.74), OpenR1-Math (0.86), DeepMath-309K (0.86), dart-math-hard (1.06), Maths-College (1.12). Ranking agreement with target: PDA=0.636 (95% CI [0.515, 0.743]), Spearman rho=0.371 (p=0.236, not significant), Top-1=False (NLL picks mathplus, target picks dart-math-hard). NLL baseline is weaker than standard-LR proxy (PDA=0.712), confirming that fine-tuning provides ranking signal beyond base-model distributional fit. Results in EXPERIMENT_RESULTS/base_nll_baseline/ and tlr_proxy_sft/results/base_nll_ranking.json.

title: Tiny-LR Proxy SFT on Qwen2.5-1.5B (Condition B — Proposed Method)
description:
Fine-tune the proxy model Qwen2.5-1.5B on each of the 12 candidate math datasets using a tiny learning rate (5e-6, one order of magnitude smaller than the standard 5e-5), then evaluate on GSM8K and MATH-500 to produce proxy scores S_p(D_i; eta_tiny). This is the core proposed method (Condition B): the hypothesis is that training proxy SFT runs at a tiny learning rate keeps the model in a near-linear regime where changes in downstream evaluation are dominated by first-order gradient alignment, yielding dataset rankings that better match the target model's ranking than standard-LR proxy runs. The tiny LR value 5e-6 is itself the standard full-finetuning LR for Qwen2.5 in OpenDataArena's Table 2, making it a natural anchor — applied here to LoRA proxy training where the standard LoRA SFT LR is 5e-5. All other training hyperparameters are identical to the Standard-LR Proxy baseline to ensure a fair single-variable comparison. The resulting ranking is compared against target ground-truth to compute PDA and Spearman correlation.

Key reference codebase: LLaMA-Factory (https://github.com/hiyouga/LlamaFactory) — reuse the same training infrastructure and configs as the Standard-LR Proxy baseline, changing only the learning_rate field.
summary: Completed tiny-LR proxy SFT (LR=5e-6) on Qwen2.5-1.5B across 12 datasets x 3 seeds. All 36 training runs, merges, and evaluations completed. Ranking agreement vs target: PDA=0.349 (95% CI [0.242, 0.470]), Spearman rho=-0.378 (p=0.226), Top-1=False. Hypothesis NOT supported: tiny-LR proxy performs worse than standard-LR proxy (PDA=0.712) and base NLL baseline (PDA=0.636). Loss diagnostics show non-degenerate training (avg 16.4% loss drop). Results saved to EXPERIMENT_RESULTS/tiny_lr_proxy_sft/.

title: Effectiveness Evaluation: Tiny-LR Proxy SFT Dataset Ranking Transfer
description: Evaluate whether the proposed Tiny-LR Proxy SFT method (Condition B) is effective at producing dataset rankings that better match the target model's ground-truth ranking compared to baselines. The evaluation compares PDA, Spearman rho, and Top-1 accuracy across three methods: (1) Standard-LR Proxy SFT (Condition A), (2) Training-Free Base-Model NLL (Condition C), and (3) Tiny-LR Proxy SFT (Condition B, proposed). A random-ranking baseline (PDA=0.5, Spearman=0.0) serves as a sanity check. Success requires: PDA(tiny) > PDA(standard) with the improvement outside the bootstrap 95% CI, PDA(standard) > 0.55, and non-degenerate tiny-LR runs (verified via loss-drop and KL checks).
summary: Effectiveness evaluation completed. Verdict: bad. Tiny-LR Proxy SFT (best config: LR=1e-5, 1000 steps) achieves composite PDA=0.500 (random-level), substantially worse than Standard-LR Proxy PDA=0.712 and Training-Free NLL PDA=0.636. Pre-registered refute criterion met: PDA(tiny) <= PDA(standard). MATH-500-only PDA is competitive (0.818 vs 0.864) but GSM8K collapses (0.515 vs 0.667) due to response-length confound. Hypothesis refuted on composite metric. Results: EXPERIMENT_RESULTS/effectiveness_evaluation_result.json, effectiveness_evaluation_report.md, tlr_proxy_sft/results/main_results_table.csv, per_benchmark_pda.json.

title: Learning Rate Sensitivity Ablation (Mid-LR Proxy)
description: Investigate how proxy-to-target ranking transfer varies as a function of the proxy learning rate by adding an intermediate LR point (2e-5) between the standard (5e-5) and tiny (5e-6) regimes. This ablation tests whether ranking transfer improves monotonically as LR decreases, or whether there is a non-trivial transition point. Together with the Standard-LR and Tiny-LR results, this provides three points on the LR-vs-PDA curve, helping characterize the relationship and informing practical LR selection guidelines.

title: Non-Degeneracy Diagnostics and Training Dynamics Analysis
description: Verify that Tiny-LR proxy runs are not degenerate (i.e., 'tiny LR = no training') by measuring training loss drop and KL divergence between the fine-tuned proxy and the base checkpoint. This analysis addresses Confound 1 from the experimental rigor section: if KL < 1e-4 nats/token AND loss drop < 0.5%, the run is labeled degenerate and results are treated as inconclusive. Additionally, compare training dynamics (loss curves, KL trajectories) across Standard-LR and Tiny-LR regimes to provide insight into how the learning rate affects optimization behavior during SFT.
